Subject: HarborTech on-prem cluster kickoff — initial env details

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick follow-up with the facts from our side to start the provisioning discussion:

- Primary site: Seattle datacenter (racked colocation)
- Expected steady-state Q3 traffic: ~80 concurrent requests/sec (model mix: 60% embeddings, 40% generation)
- Desired latency SLO: 95th <= 300ms for generation requests (p50 much lower)
- Disk profile: mixed NVMe SSDs for GPU hosts, spinning archive for long-term artifacts

Key asks from HarborTech:
1) A recommended nodeclass breakdown for control, inference (GPU), and batch jobs (CPU)
2) PV strategy to avoid eviction of large KV caches and artifacts during bursts
3) Guidance whether to co-locate smaller CPU batch pods on GPU nodes or use separate nodepools

I've attached our internal capacity spreadsheet. Can your team propose a starting nodeclass map and IO topology we can iterate on?

Alex

Alex — thanks for the detail, this is a good starting point. Attaching a draft nodeclass/IO map and a short MAPlan to align on next steps. High-level notes below; we'll follow with a proposed playbook entry for provisioning.

High-level proposal (first pass):
- control-plane: 3 x m5.large-equivalent VMs (high availability + API responsiveness)
- gpu-inference nodeclass (inference-high): NVMe-backed instances (8x A10 / equivalent) with local SSD for KV cache and model shards; use dedicated RAID for local checkpointing
- gpu-burst nodeclass (inference-burst): smaller GPU instances for burst/low-cost variants (quantized runtime) with network-attached SSD to reduce single-host rebuild time
- cpu-batch nodeclass: c5-like instances with EBS/attachable network storage for heavy preprocessing and offline jobs

Storage/IO considerations:
- KV caches should use local, high-IO NVMe with a tolerated working set replication across 2 nodes to avoid cold-start latency spikes.
- Model artifacts (immutable) should be on a read-optimized NFS/object store with aggressive caching tier on NVMe.
- Pod eviction policy: reserve 25% headroom on inference nodes for autoscaling spikes; use taints/tolerations for best-effort batch jobs.

Next steps:
- Dev to sketch exact CPU/GPU counts and PV classes (I copied you on the doc).
- Schedule a short topology review (30m) — propose Tue 5/20 10am PT.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: HarborTech on-prem cluster kickoff — nodeclass & IO topology (technical notes)

Looping in a few low-level constraints I want us to call out explicitly for the topology review:

1) PersistentVolumes & eviction:
- Use two PV classes: fast-local (local-NVMe CSI) and net-read (NFS/objectfuse). fast-local for KV cache with reclaimPolicy: Retain and node-affinity to keep caches hot; net-read for model blobs.
- Consider using emptyDir with size-limited tmpfs for ephemeral tokenizer caches to reduce IO load on persistent stores.

2) Pod placement and throughput shaping:
- Node selectors: inference-high nodes should expose the GPU capability label (gpu=true) and nvme=true.
- Use kube-batch/VerticalPodAutoscaler for batch window scheduling; reserve CPU shares for inference svc.

3) Data durability vs. restart times:
- For smaller models (<10GB) we recommend eager local prefetch on pod start (model pull to local NVMe) to keep inference latency predictable. For larger models, run model-server from networked object storage with aggressive local kernel cache pinning.

4) Network egress and cross-datacenter fallback:
- Define explicit egress routing to Redwood control plane for metrics only. All inference tokens stay local. Add a fallback policy to route to Redwood-hosted model variant if local capacity is saturated.

I'll prepare a sizing table with vCPU/GPU counts and expected eviction thresholds by tomorrow for the meeting.

—Dev
